brief: Goldman's GSXUCEXP Consumer Experiences Basket has underperformed the SPXXAI Index by 14% even though experience spending growth accelerated from 1% in Q1 2025 to 6% in Q1 2026, versus 2% for broader services. That gap, plus attractive valuations, earnings revisions nearing inflection, and positioning that is not overly crowded, is why GS recommends buying the basket. Higher fuel costs have hurt Consumer, the worst-performing sector on GS's monitor year to date, but the basket's skew to higher-income consumers should leave it insulated whether oil stays elevated or de-escalates. The basket's recent negative correlation with AI is expected to turn more positive as demand for experiences that cannot be replicated digitally rises, echoing the shift to physical and social activity after peak Metaverse hype in 2021. Company commentary across live entertainment, theme parks, hotels and cruises (DIS, LYV, TKO, MSGS, SPHR, MAR, HLT, CCL, RCL, VIK, NCLH, among others) reinforces the bullish case ahead of earnings season. Trade vehicle: a GSXUCEXP 15Jan27 110%/120% call spread costing 1.61% (ref 91.12), buying 25.21-vol 24-delta and selling 23.73-vol 7-delta, for 6.2x max payout and an 11.61% breakeven.
